note: Pet Peeves, content v3 (10 words). Course level B1.1 (Gateway level 9), unit Pet Peeves, from the Anki Pet-Peeves export.

words.meaning: People who tell others how to behave but don't follow their own advice.
situations: My uncle tells everyone to stop smoking, but he smokes a pack a day himself.
Our boss shouts at us for being late, then walks in at ten every morning.
gaps: I can't stand ______ who tell you to save money while they waste theirs.
Politicians who talk about saving water but fill their huge pools are ______.
Don't be one of those ______ who say 'be kind online' and then post mean comments.
hints: They say one thing and do the opposite.
Starts with 'hypo-'; the singular ends in '-crite'.

commonMistakes.why: 'Hypocrisy' is the behaviour; the person is a 'hypocrite'.

words.meaning: Charging much higher prices than normal for things people badly need, especially during a shortage or emergency.
situations: During the storm, the shop near my house sold bottles of water for five times what they normally cost.
When everyone needed face masks, some websites sold a box for $80 instead of $5.
gaps: The store was fined for ______ after it tripled the cost of water during the flood.
Charging crazy amounts for medicine during a crisis is ______.
The government passed a law against ______ during emergencies.
hints: Raising prices unfairly when people have no choice.
Two words: 'price' + a word meaning to overcharge.

commonMistakes.sentence: The shop did a price gouge on water.
commonMistakes.correction: The shop was accused of price gouging on water.
commonMistakes.why: Use the noun phrase 'price gouging' (or the verb 'gouge customers').

words.meaning: Describes a person who gets angry very quickly, even about small things — it's part of their personality.
situations: My neighbour starts shouting the moment a child's ball touches his car — he's been like that for years.
Our old coach lost his patience with players over tiny mistakes in every single practice.
gaps: He's very ______ — he loses his patience over the smallest thing.
Don't argue with her; she's ______ and will start shouting.
Working long hours made him tired and ______.
hints: Gets angry quickly as a personality trait — the opposite of patient.
Two words with a hyphen: 'short' + a word for mood.

words.meaning: Eating without closing your lips, so other people can see the food in your mouth.
situations: At dinner, my cousin talked while eating, and everyone could see the half-eaten rice in his mouth.
My mum always tells my little brother, 'Close your lips when you eat!'
gaps: ______ is considered very rude at the table.
My biggest pet peeve at restaurants is ______ — I don't want to see your food.
Kids need to learn that ______ is bad table manners.
hints: A table-manners problem you can see, not just hear.
Starts with 'Chewing with…'.

commonMistakes.correction: He chews with his mouth open.
commonMistakes.why: Say 'with his/your mouth open' — the possessive is needed.

words.meaning: People who don't keep their body, hands or space clean.
situations: My roommate never washes his hands after the bathroom and leaves dirty plates for days.
On the hot bus, a man who clearly hadn't showered for a week sat next to me.
gaps: ______ who don't wash their hands after the bathroom really annoy me.
Sharing a kitchen with ______ is a nightmare.
The gym asked members to wipe the machines because of a few ______.
hints: People who aren't clean — the opposite of 'hygienic'.
The adjective starts with 'un-'.

commonMistakes.why: The adjective is 'unhygienic'; 'hygiene' is the noun.

words.meaning: Speaking to people in short, sharp, angry words, usually because you are tired or stressed.
situations: When I asked my sister a simple question this morning, she answered 'What?! I'm busy!' and turned away.
Dad didn't sleep last night, so every time we talked to him, he answered in one rude word.
gaps: She was ______ with everyone at work today because she didn't sleep well.
Sorry I was ______ on the phone — I was really stressed.
Don't be so ______ with the waiter; it's not his fault.
hints: About how you talk: quick, sharp, irritated replies.
From the verb 'snap' + '-y'.

commonMistakes.correction: She was snappy with me. / She snapped at me.
commonMistakes.why: 'Snappy' is an adjective; the verb is 'snap at someone'.

words.meaning: Workers who prepare or serve food with their bare hands instead of wearing gloves.
situations: The man at the sandwich shop took my money, then made my sandwich with the same bare hands.
At the bakery, the worker picked up my croissant with her bare fingers instead of using tongs.
gaps: ______ are one of my biggest pet peeves — it just feels unsafe.
The restaurant was fined because inspectors saw ______ touching raw meat and salad.
I stopped eating at that burger place because of the ______.
hints: Kitchen workers with no gloves on.
Starts with 'Glove-' and ends with 'handlers'.

commonMistakes.why: The adjective is 'gloveless' (no 's' in the middle).

words.meaning: In a bad, complaining mood — quietly annoyed and unfriendly, but not shouting.
situations: Every morning before his coffee, my dad sits at the table, frowns and complains about everything.
The old man next door never smiles and moans about the weather, the noise and the neighbours.
gaps: He's always ______ before he's had his morning coffee.
Why are you so ______ today? You haven't smiled once.
My cat gets ______ when I wake her up.
hints: A bad, complaining mood — like one of the seven dwarfs.
Rhymes with 'lumpy'.

commonMistakes.why: After 'is', use the adjective 'grumpy'; 'grumpily' is an adverb.

words.meaning: To make someone very annoyed or angry (informal and a bit rude — use with friends, not at work).
situations: It really makes me mad when people take my parking spot after I've been waiting with my signal on.
My friend keeps borrowing my charger and never gives it back, and I'm sick of it.
gaps: It really ______ when people cut in line.
Stop doing that — you're going to ______!
Nothing ______ more than slow Wi-Fi.
hints: A rude informal way to say 'make someone very angry'.
Phrasal verb with 'off'; the adjective is '___ed off'.

commonMistakes.why: With a pronoun, it goes in the middle: piss me off.

words.meaning: People who talk during a film at the cinema and spoil it for everyone else.
situations: The couple behind us in the cinema discussed their weekend plans through the whole film.
A man in the front row kept explaining the story to his friend in a loud voice.
gaps: ______ are one of my biggest pet peeves — I paid to hear the film, not their chat.
The cinema shows a 'please be quiet' message to stop ______.
I prefer watching films at home, away from ______.
hints: Cinema-goers who chat during the film.
Two words: 'movie' + people who talk.

commonMistakes.why: Use the plural 'talkers' for more than one person.
